preference-relation.name: Preference relation
preference-relation.sym: ≿
def: Preference relation: reflexive, complete and transitive

preference-questionnaire.name: Preferences as questionnaire answers (Definition 1)
preference-questionnaire.sym: f
preference-questionnaire.gloss: Preferences are answers to every question “how do you compare x and y?” that do not depend on the order of the question and chain consistently across triples.
def: Preferences as consistent answers to a questionnaire

completeness.name: Completeness
def: Preference relation: reflexive, complete and transitive

reflexivity.name: Reflexivity
def: Preference relation: reflexive, complete and transitive

transitivity.name: Transitivity
def: Preference relation: reflexive, complete and transitive

utility-representation.name: Utility representation
utility-representation.sym: u
def: Utility function representing a preference relation

continuous-utility-representation.name: Continuous utility representation
def: Utility function representing a preference relation

lexicographic-preference.name: Lexicographic preference
lexicographic-preference.sym: ≿L​
lexicographic-preference.gloss: Given a ranked list of preferences, the lexicographic preference compares two alternatives by the first preference in the list that tells them apart.
def: Lexicographic preference induced by a list of preferences

continuity.name: Continuity of preferences (C1, open balls)
continuity.gloss: A preference is continuous if, whenever a is strictly preferred to b, every point near a is strictly preferred to every point near b.

continuity-closed-graph.name: Continuity of preferences (C2, closed graph)
continuity-closed-graph.gloss: A preference is continuous if its graph is closed: when comparisons hold along converging sequences, they hold at the limits as well.

context.name: Context (grand set and domain of choice problems)
context.sym: (X,D)
context.gloss: A context (X, D) fixes the grand set X and the collection D of choice problems, nonempty subsets of X, on which behavior is observed.
def: Choice problems and the domain of a choice context

choice-function.name: Choice function
choice-function.sym: C
choice-function.gloss: A choice function assigns to each choice problem in its domain a single element of that problem.

induced-choice-function.name: Choice function induced by a preference (rational choice)
induced-choice-function.sym: C≿​
induced-choice-function.gloss: When every choice problem has a unique best element under a preference relation, the rational choice function picks that element.
def: The choice function induced by a preference relation

rationalizable.name: Rationalizable choice function
rationalizable.gloss: A choice function can be rationalized if some preference relation induces it: from every problem in the domain it picks the unique best element.

condition-alpha.name: Condition α (choice functions)
condition-alpha.sym: α
condition-alpha.gloss: If the element chosen from a set belongs to a smaller set, it is also the element chosen from the smaller set.

satisficing-choice-function.name: Satisficing choice function
satisficing-choice-function.sym: Cv,v∗,O​
satisficing-choice-function.gloss: Satisficing (Simon): examine alternatives in a fixed order and pick the first one that meets a threshold; if none does, pick the last one examined.

choice-correspondence.name: Choice correspondence
choice-correspondence.sym: C
choice-correspondence.gloss: A choice correspondence assigns to each choice problem a nonempty subset of it: the alternatives that may be chosen.

induced-choice-correspondence.name: Choice correspondence induced by a preference
induced-choice-correspondence.sym: C≿​
induced-choice-correspondence.gloss: The rational choice correspondence picks the set of best elements of each problem, assumed never to be empty.
def: The choice correspondence induced by a preference relation

weak-axiom.name: Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (choice correspondences)
weak-axiom.sym: WA
weak-axiom.gloss: If x and y are both available in A and in B, x is chosen from A and y is chosen from B, then x is also chosen from B.
def: The weak axiom of revealed preference (WA)

condition-alpha-correspondence.name: Condition α (choice correspondences)
condition-alpha-correspondence.sym: α
condition-alpha-correspondence.gloss: An alternative chosen from a set is also chosen from every smaller set in the domain that contains it.

condition-beta.name: Condition β (choice correspondences)
condition-beta.sym: β
condition-beta.gloss: If a and b are both chosen from a set and b is chosen from a larger set, then a is chosen from the larger set as well.

rationalizable-correspondence.name: Rationalizable choice correspondence
def: Conditions α and β imply rationalizability of a correspondence

extended-choice-function.name: Extended choice function (choice with a default)
extended-choice-function.sym: c(A,a)
extended-choice-function.gloss: Choice problems with a default: for every set and every default in it, an extended choice function picks one element of the set.

default-bias-procedure.name: Default-bias procedure
default-bias-procedure.sym: DBPu,β​
default-bias-procedure.gloss: Switch to the best non-default alternative only if its utility exceeds the default’s utility plus a bias bonus; otherwise keep the default.

weak-axiom-default.name: Weak Axiom for choice with a default
weak-axiom-default.sym: WA
weak-axiom-default.gloss: WA rules out two patterns of reversal between distinct alternatives a and b that are available in two sets.
def: The weak axiom for choice with defaults

default-tendency.name: Default Tendency
default-tendency.sym: DT
default-tendency.gloss: If a is chosen from A when x is the default, then a is still chosen from A when a itself is the default.

monotonicity.name: Monotonicity
monotonicity.gloss: More of every good is at least as good, and strictly more of every good is strictly better.

strong-monotonicity.name: Strong monotonicity
strong-monotonicity.gloss: A bundle with at least as much of every good, and different from the other bundle, is strictly better.

strong-monotonicity-commodity-1.name: Strong monotonicity in commodity 1
def: Every bundle without good 1 is worth some amount of good 1

nonsatiation.name: Nonsatiation at a bundle
nonsatiation.gloss: A preference is nonsatiated at a bundle if arbitrarily close to it there is a strictly better bundle.

continuity-orthant.name: Continuity on the commodity space (single radius)
continuity-orthant.gloss: If a is strictly preferred to b, then for some radius every bundle that close to a is strictly preferred to every bundle that close to b.
def: Continuous preferences on the commodity space

continuity-real-line.name: Continuity of a preference on the real line
def: A continuous, convex preference on ℝ with no concave utility

continuity-unit-interval.name: Continuity of a preference on [0, 1]
def: For continuous preferences on an interval, single-peakedness is Λ-strict convexity

convexity.name: Convexity (Convexity 1)
convexity.gloss: If x is at least as good as y, then every mixture of x and y is at least as good as y.

convexity-2.name: Convexity 2 (a mixture is at least as good as one endpoint)
convexity-2.gloss: A mixture z of two bundles x and y is at least as good as one of them.

convexity-3.name: Convexity 3 (convex upper contour sets)
convexity-3.gloss: For every bundle y, the set of bundles at least as good as y is convex.

convexity-real-line.name: Convexity of a preference on the real line
def: A continuous, convex preference on ℝ with no concave utility

lambda-convexity.name: Lambda-convexity (book definition)
lambda-convexity.sym: Λ
lambda-convexity.gloss: A preference is Λ-convex if, at every alternative, improving on it requires advancing some criterion from the family Λ.

psi-convexity.name: Ψ-convexity (algebraic linear orderings)
psi-convexity.sym: Ψ
psi-convexity.gloss: For a nonzero value vector v, bundles are ranked by their value v·x; Ψ is the family of all such orderings.

bottom-up-constructible.name: Constructible by the bottom-up placement procedure
def: On a finite set, Λ-convex preferences are built from the bottom up

strict-convexity.name: Strict convexity
strict-convexity.gloss: If two distinct bundles are each at least as good as y, every strict mixture of them is strictly better than y.

lambda-strict-convexity.name: Lambda-strict convexity
lambda-strict-convexity.sym: Λ
lambda-strict-convexity.gloss: Λ-strict convexity requires one criterion to advance for every move to another alternative that is at least as good.

single-peaked.name: Single-peaked preference on [0, 1]
single-peaked.gloss: A preference on [0, 1] is single-peaked if it has a unique best point and falls off strictly on both sides of it.

quasiconcave-utility.name: Quasi-concave utility function
def: Convex preferences are exactly those with quasi-concave utility

concave-utility-representation.name: Concave utility representation
def: A continuous, convex preference on ℝ with no concave utility

homotheticity.name: Homotheticity
homotheticity.gloss: A preference is homothetic if scaling two bundles by the same factor never reverses their comparison.

homogeneous-utility-representation.name: Continuous utility representation homogeneous of degree one
def: Continuous, monotone homothetic preferences have a degree-one homogeneous utility

quasi-linearity.name: Quasi-linearity in commodity 1
quasi-linearity.gloss: A preference is quasi-linear in good 1 if adding the same amount of good 1 to two bundles never reverses their comparison.

quasi-linearity-all.name: Quasi-linearity in all commodities
quasi-linearity-all.gloss: Adding the same amount of any one good to two bundles never reverses their comparison.

quasi-linear-utility-representation.name: Quasi-linear utility representation
def: A utility linear in good 1 for quasi-linear preferences

linear-utility-representation.name: Linear utility representation with positive weights
linear-utility-representation.sym: u(x)=α⋅x
def: Continuous, strongly monotone preferences quasi-linear in every good have a linear utility

differentiability.name: Differentiable preference
differentiability.gloss: A preference is differentiable at x if its improvement directions are exactly the directions with positive value under some marginal-value vector.

improvement-direction-set.name: Set of improvement directions
improvement-direction-set.sym: D≿​(x)
improvement-direction-set.gloss: A change z improves on x if x + z is strictly better; a direction is an improvement direction if every small enough step along it is an improvement.

value-direction-set.name: Directions valued positively by a value function
value-direction-set.sym: Dv​(x)
value-direction-set.gloss: Given subjective marginal values v(x), a feasible direction d counts as an improvement when its value-weighted change d·v(x) is positive.
def: Improvement directions according to subjective values

budget-set.name: Budget set
budget-set.sym: B(p,w)
def: Continuous preferences guarantee a solution to the consumer problem

demand-existence.name: Every consumer problem has a solution
def: Continuous preferences guarantee a solution to the consumer problem

demand-convex-valued.name: Convex set of solutions of the consumer problem
def: Convexity and uniqueness of the consumer’s optimum

demand-uniqueness.name: At most one solution of the consumer problem
def: Convexity and uniqueness of the consumer’s optimum

walras-law.name: Walras’ law (demand exhausts wealth)
walras-law.sym: p⋅x=w
def: Walras’ law: monotone consumers exhaust their budget

demand-continuity.name: Continuity of the demand function in prices and wealth

demand-closed-graph.name: Closed graph of the demand correspondence
def: The demand correspondence has a closed graph

weak-axiom-demand.name: Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (demand functions)
weak-axiom-demand.sym: WA

indirect-preference.name: Indirect preference over choice problems
indirect-preference.sym: ≿∗
indirect-preference.gloss: One menu is indirectly preferred to another when the element chosen from it is at least as good as the element chosen from the other.

indirect-utility.name: Indirect utility over choice problems
indirect-utility.gloss: If u represents the preference, the indirect utility of a menu is the utility of the element chosen from it.
def: Indirect utility of a choice set

budget-indirect-preference.name: Indirect preference over budget parameters
budget-indirect-preference.sym: (p,w)≿∗(p′,w′)
budget-indirect-preference.gloss: One price–wealth pair is indirectly preferred to another when the bundle demanded at the first is at least as good as the bundle demanded at the second.

demand-function.sym: x(p,w)
def: The demand: solution of the prime problem

prime-problem-solution.name: Solution of the prime problem (best bundle in the budget set)
def: The demand: solution of the prime problem

dual-problem-solution.name: Solution of the dual problem (cheapest bundle at least as good as z)

hicksian-demand.name: Hicksian demand and the expenditure function
hicksian-demand.sym: h(p,z), e(p,z)

pareto.name: Pareto condition (Par)
